note: Saladin's unification of Egypt and Syria put the Kingdom of Jerusalem in an existential strategic bind; Hattin (1187) and the fall of Jerusalem define this rivalry. After Saladin's death, intermittent warfare and diplomacy including the Sixth Crusade's negotiated return of Jerusalem (1229–1244) continued under his successors.

_quarry.structural_significance: Saladin's recapture of Jerusalem (1187) eliminated the political rationale for the First Crusader Kingdom and forced the reconfiguration of the Crusader presence to coastal enclaves; the subsequent Treaty of Jaffa (1229) demonstrated that accommodation rather than reconquest was the sustainable model, reshaping crusading ideology toward diplomatic engagement.
